name: Split Cord Malformation Type I

criteria.description: Presence of a rigid osseocartilaginous septum dividing the spinal cord into two hemicords
Each hemicord contained within its own dural sac
Neurological deficits consistent with tethered cord or spinal cord malformation
MRI or CT evidence of split cord with bony spur

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Identification of a rigid osseocartilaginous septum dividing the spinal cord into two hemicords with two dural sacs on imaging
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily radiological; clinical symptoms vary depending on severity and associated anomalies.

imaging: MRI demonstrating two hemicords separated by a bony or cartilaginous spur
CT scan showing osseous septum dividing the spinal canal
Ultrasound in infants may show split cord features
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; considered a congenital malformation with multifactorial etiology
other: Intraoperative findings confirm presence of bony spur and two dural sacs

distinguishingFeatures: Single dural sac containing both hemicords
Absence of bony or cartilaginous septum
More flexible fibrous septum instead of rigid spur
Neurological symptoms without anatomical division of cord
MRI shows low-lying conus medullaris without bony spur

redFlags: Progressive lower limb weakness or paralysis
Rapid onset bladder or bowel dysfunction
Severe back pain with neurological deficits
references: Mahapatra AK, Gupta DK. Split cord malformations: a clinical study of 254 patients and a proposal for a new clinical-imaging classification. J Neurosurg Pediatr. 2005;102(2):131-139.
Pang D, Dias MS, Ahab-Barmada M. Split cord malformation: Part I: A unified theory of embryogenesis for double spinal cord malformations. Neurosurgery. 1992;31(3):451-480.
Orphanet: Split cord malformation type I - ORPHA:1671
